Given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{2}{7},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{2}{7},$ where $\theta =m∠B.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{BC}$ adjacent to $∠B.$ Hence, we can use the cosine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{2}{7} & =\frac{4}{AB} \\ AB & =\frac{4}{2}\cdot 7 \\ AB & =14\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find the missing side $AC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{14}^{2}-{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{196-16} \\  & =\sqrt{180} \\  & =6\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\sqrt{5}\cdot 4 \\  & =12\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
